open_issues: Low finding on .gitignore (artifacts/ untracked) NOT fixed: .gitignore is outside this package's allowed paths (tests/Wakeel.E2E, build/e2e.ps1, src/Wakeel.Desktop only), exactly as the review itself noted ('needs supervisor approval rather than a builder edit'). Someone with access to .gitignore should add a 'tests/Wakeel.E2E/artifacts/' line.

The medium finding's suggested W08ScreenshotDiff fix (Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride + page.ScreenshotAsync) was verified NOT sufficient on this machine: with a CDP-attached (not Playwright-launched) page, Playwright's own ScreenshotAsync pipeline resets emulation from its internally-tracked (unset) viewport state, so the capture stayed at the host's native physical size (1708x960 on this 125%-scaled display) despite the override. Fixed instead by calling 'Page.captureScreenshot' directly on the CDP session after the override, bypassing Playwright's screenshot pipeline entirely -- verified this reliably produces an exact 1366x768 PNG across two full runs. Flagging in case another reviewer wants to double check this on a different WebView2/Playwright version.

Unrelated to this package, not touched: two untracked Word files at the repo root (a '.docx' and, this session, a differently-named one than last review's '~$...' lock file) -- Word has/had a document open there; nothing to do with Wakeel.E2E, flagged only so they are not swept into any future commit.
notes:
Applied every high/medium/low finding and both missing-spec items from the review.

HIGH -- start-url origin escape (src/Wakeel.Desktop/MainWindow.xaml.cs, ConfigureStartUrl): tightened the guard exactly as prescribed (reject empty path, missing leading '/', protocol-relative '//..', any backslash form, and anything Uri.TryCreate(path, UriKind.Relative) rejects). Re-verified live with the reviewer's own PoC: `Start-Process ... --remote-debugging-port=9444 --start-url=//localhost:9600/probe` against a real loopback TcpListener on 127.0.0.1:9600 -- NO connection arrived within 15s (previously the WebView2 connected out), and /json/list showed the CDP target on the app's own default route (https://0.0.0.1/gallery), not about:blank and not the attacker host. Control run with --start-url=/w08 (via PowerShell, to avoid Git-Bash's POSIX-path mangling of a bare leading '/') correctly resolved to https://0.0.0.1/w08, confirming legitimate routes still work.

MEDIUM -- W08 screenshot DPI dependency (tests/Wakeel.E2E/GalleryAndAttentionCenterTests.cs, W08ScreenshotDiff): pinned the CSS viewport via CDP Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride(1366x768, deviceScaleFactor 1) on a fresh CDP session, but discovered (and had to work around) that Playwright's own Page.ScreenshotAsync still returns the host's native physical pixels for a CDP-attached page -- verified live, it kept returning 1709x960-class images despite the override. Switched to calling Page.captureScreenshot directly on the CDP session (base64 PNG written to disk myself), which does honor the override. W08-actual.png is now exactly 1366x768 (asserted with Assert.Equal on Bitmap.Width/Height) in both final runs, on a 125%-scaled display, with no resizing/resampling needed on either the actual capture or the design export -- addresses missing_spec_item 1. Diff percentage moved from the reviewed run's 34.1035% (which came from upscaling the tiny design export onto a distorted 1709x960 target) to 33.3045% (genuine 1366x768-vs-1366x768 comparison, no resampling) -- this is the corrected, comparable figure, not a regression.

MEDIUM -- port collision / stale-instance ambiguity (tests/Wakeel.E2E/Support/LaunchedWakeelApp.cs, WakeelE2eFixture.cs): (a) StartAsync now probes http://127.0.0.1:{pollPort}/json/version before Process.Start and throws WakeelAppLaunchException naming the port if anything already answers, refusing to start a second instance. Verified live: manually started a leftover Wakeel.Desktop.exe on port 9333, then ran the full test suite -- it failed fast with 'Refusing to start Wakeel.Desktop.exe: ... already answers ... Kill it and retry.' on every test that uses the fixture, instead of silently sharing the WebView2 profile with the stale process. (b) WakeelE2eFixture.WaitForPageAsync now takes the expected start route and matches on AbsolutePath (browser.Contexts...Pages.FirstOrDefault(p => new Uri(p.Url).AbsolutePath == expectedPath)) instead of blind FirstOrDefault(), failing with the list of observed URLs on timeout -- a second line of defense behind (a).

LOW -- WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS from inherited environment (src/Wakeel.Desktop/App.xaml.cs, ConfigureRemoteDebugging): now calls Environment.SetEnvironmentVariable(..., null) unconditionally at the top of the method before any flag parsing, so an inherited value can never contribute switches; only a validated --remote-debugging-port from this process's own argv sets it again.

LOW -- process leaks on cancellation / no Process.Dispose (tests/Wakeel.E2E/Support/LaunchedWakeelApp.cs): the whole body after Process.Start is now wrapped in try { ... } catch { await KillAsync(process); process.Dispose(); throw; }, so a cancelled cancellationToken (or any other exception) kills and disposes the process before propagating instead of leaking it; the inner TaskCanceledException catch in the readiness poll now has a `when (!cancellationToken.IsCancellationRequested)` guard so a genuine cancellation is no longer silently swallowed by the polling branch. DisposeAsync also now calls _process.Dispose() after KillAsync.

LOW -- W08ScreenshotDiff permanently leaves the developer's real ui-state.json on 'light' (WakeelE2eFixture.cs, GalleryAndAttentionCenterTests.cs): took the reviewer's 'better' option -- WakeelE2eFixture.InitializeAsync now captures the html[data-theme] attribute once, right after startup, and DisposeAsync restores exactly that theme (clicking the matching Ar.Gallery.Theme* tab) before killing the app, covering every test in the class in one place. Removed the redundant per-test try/finally from ThemeToggles (now dead code once centralized) and W08ScreenshotDiff needed none added. Verified live: manually set %LocalAppData%\Wakeel\ui-state.json to {"theme":"dark"}, ran the full suite (which flips through dark/light along the way), and confirmed the file read back {"theme":"dark"} afterward -- restored, not reset to a hardcoded "system".

LOW -- tautological Assert.InRange(percentage, 0, 100) (GalleryAndAttentionCenterTests.cs): replaced with Assert.True(File.Exists(diffPath)) and Assert.Equal(percentage.ToString("F4"), File.ReadAllText(percentagePath)), asserting the artefacts the spec actually asks for; the _output.WriteLine recording is unchanged.
